http_contract: 0.4.2; production implementation unchanged in this test iteration

hardware.execution: Go API/load generator/SDK on Windows; native Centrifugo on Windows; PostgreSQL 18.6 in Docker Linux temporary memory storage

scope.tested: threaded posts: root entries, one-level replies, quotes of roots and children, history reads, authorized HTTPS writes and native WSS deliveries
scope.stages: P2 backend complete; P3 business not started; P6 production capacity not accepted

harness_revisions.final_run: Same inputs and production sources; cleanup frees completed peers receive maps and drops phase correlation maps before the next scenario. Final source fingerprints below.

notes: Three four-stage runs; two original runs and one cleanup-corrected run. Each topology creates new distinct-subject WSS connections sequentially before traffic. Warmup 3 seconds, measured launch window 12 seconds.

Hot input uses a fixed arrival schedule with 32 workers per topic; ordinary reads stay 100/s with 32 workers, ordinary writes 25/s with 8 workers. Every failed started attempt remains in HTTP latency.
Writes cycle root entry, child quoting root, child quoting child. All are actual threaded-mode requests, not relabeled chat/instant-channel traffic.
Clients and API share a Go process and physical machine. WSS callbacks decode/validate payloads; this measurement does not isolate production server CPU from generator cost.
Send-to-receive is measured by the same Go monotonic clock, includes HTTP admission/transaction, native consumption, WSS transport and SDK callback scheduling. It is not commit-to-delivery time.
Expected fanout uses actual database commits and actual subscriber count, never offered-but-unsent or refused writes. The input deficits and HTTP 503 counts remain explicit.

After input stops, await HTTP completions and check database rows; then drain outbox/client callbacks for at most 30 seconds. delivery_drain_ms covers only that final wait, not the whole post-window interval.
API pool is 16; global transaction budget 12; 2 per counter and 256 total admitted/waiting commands. Stat probe and aggregate observer use separate 1-connection fixture pools; observation adds load.
Native outbox consumer stays one partition with 20ms polling, memory broker, history size 2/TTL 60s. No production tuning, dependency upgrade or business change was used to hide overload.
The initial probe attempted a query beyond the API role and was refused. The final harness uses the existing aggregate-only observer role; API privileges were not expanded.
Token refresh callbacks use the real HTTPS endpoint; measured runs reported zero refreshes/reconnects. This is not a reconnect-storm, slow-reader or refresh-capacity benchmark.
Only synthetic aggregate telemetry is retained: no bodies, tokens, database URLs, actor IDs, resource IDs or event IDs.

verification.final_fanout_run: passed, test 98.43s; measured input demand deliberately includes HTTP 503 and unsent arrivals, not capacity acceptance
verification.full_regression: passed, postgres package 88.972s; includes 65-second real outage and cache expiry
